goal: Deploy a SIG v2 observer node as a real Kurtosis container on this host and capture honest machine-readable evidence of where it lands (the user's actual ask: 'deploy a zig testnet node using container in a kurtosis based testnet').
method: Built the SIG v2 binary natively for aarch64-linux-gnu.2.36 (native arm64 builder avoids the Zig 0.15.2 build_runner PRNG mis-emulation under Rosetta; -Dtarget selects aarch64, the builder's own arch, so the output is a native aarch64 ELF). Runtime stage is linux/arm64 (native, no Rosetta). Ran the Kurtosis real-run probe (sig-realrun-probe.star) with `kurtosis run --privileged` so that ServiceConfig(privileged=True) takes effect. The probe writes a config.zon (.sandboxing_mode=.threaded, .cluster=.testnet) + a synthetic 432000-slot leader schedule in-container, then runs `sig config.zon` via plan.exec with a timeout. A standalone io_uring probe (aarch64 static C binary calling syscall 425 io_uring_setup) was copied into the running container to capture decisive machine-readable proof of the io_uring gate resolution.
result: PARTIAL — `started` (services boot past config parse AND past the io_uring gate, inside a real Kurtosis container).

iouring_gate_resolution.symptom_on_x86_64_rosetta: io_uring_setup (syscall 425) returns ENOSYS (38) under default, seccomp=unconfined, AND --privileged — OrbStack's Rosetta amd64 syscall-translation layer does NOT translate io_uring syscalls, even though __arm64_sys_io_uring_* ARE in /proc/kallsyms (149 symbols). Zig's IoUring.zig:62 maps .NOSYS => error.SystemOutdated, so accounts_db crashes at init. NOT solvable by privilege — the Rosetta translation layer is the gate. This caps the x86_64 image at `built`.
iouring_gate_resolution.symptom_on_native_arm64_default: io_uring_setup returns EPERM under the default container seccomp profile.
iouring_gate_resolution.resolution_on_native_arm64_privileged: io_uring_setup returns OK (fd=3, sq_entries=8, cq_entries=16, features=0x3ffff) under --privileged. OrbStack's kernel fully supports io_uring; only the default seccomp profile blocks it (EPERM), and --privileged clears that. ALL services then boot past io_uring.
